text: Designing clean REST APIs is essential for developers who use your service. Always structure your endpoints around resources, using clear nouns like `/users` or `/orders` instead of verbs. Use proper HTTP status codes to communicate results—`200` for success, `201` for creation, `404` for missing resources, and `500` for server errors. Most importantly, keep documentation updated and easy to follow; good examples help others integrate quickly. Versioning is another key practice: adding a version number, such as `/v1/users`, prevents breaking changes for existing users when you update features. By following these habits, you make your API predictable, reliable, and a pleasure to work with.
